evidence: Unreal Engine based (needs UE + GPU); geometry/scale depend on the loaded UE environment, no native real-city ingest (arXiv:1705.05065). Wind: simSetWind() sets one world-frame NED vector in m/s, i.e. uniform, not a 4D field; weather (rain, fog, ...) are 0-1 visual effect parameters enabled via simEnableWeather (https://microsoft.github.io/AirSim/apis/). Recording API saves data only, no replay (same page). MIT licence.

WindEffects: 'wind is described as a uniform worldwide model' with low-pass/sinusoid/noise gusts; force can be scaled by a piecewise scalar field (https://gazebosim.org/api/sim/8/classgz_1_1sim_1_1systems_1_1WindEffects.html). Real terrain/buildings only as user-imported heightmaps/meshes. Energy: PX4 battery_simulator is linear drain feeding PX4 failsafes (https://github.com/PX4/PX4-Autopilot/tree/main/src/modules/simulation/battery_simulator). Browser: gzweb renders a running simulation via the websocket launcher (https://github.com/gazebo-web/gzweb). Replay: --record/--playback of entity pose state.tlog (https://gazebosim.org/api/sim/9/log.html). Physics headless on CPU; camera/GPU-lidar sensors need ogre2 rendering.

Unity rendering decoupled from physics; physics up to 200,000 Hz; RL API 'can simulate hundreds of quadrotors in parallel' (arXiv:2009.00563). No wind/weather field described. Physics can run without rendering; rendering needs Unity/GPU.

PyBullet Gymnasium envs for single/multi-agent quadcopter control; examples include downwash; tested on Intel x64 Ubuntu and Apple Silicon (https://github.com/utiasDSL/gym-pybullet-drones). No weather/energy/city features documented.

Aerodynamic wrenches and pluggable wind_profile objects (e.g. SinusoidWind) act on the vehicle; users can add a custom wind field class; batched env: 'for simulations of >1000 drones ... speedups of 25x purely on CPU' (https://github.com/spencerfolk/rotorpy; arXiv:2306.04485). No city geometry.

JAX simulator, batched n_worlds x n_drones on CPU and GPU (CPU-only pip install; 3.3-15.6 M steps/s on a Ryzen 9 CPU); paper reports 'thousands of swarms of 4000 drones each' (https://github.com/utiasDSL/crazyflow; arXiv:2606.01478). No wind/weather or city geometry documented.

Built on NVIDIA Omniverse Isaac Sim with GPU-parallelized simulation for drone RL (arXiv:2309.12825); MIT licence; maintainer notes it is no longer actively maintained (https://github.com/btx0424/OmniDrones).

Built on NVIDIA Isaac Gym; GPU geometric controllers for 'simultaneous control of thousands of multirotors'; Warp GPU ray-casting sensors; BSD-3 (https://github.com/ntnu-arl/aerial_gym_simulator; doi:10.1109/LRA.2025.3548507).

Isaac Sim extension for real-time simulation of multiple multirotors in photo-realistic environments with PX4/ROS 2 integration; paper demo uses two drones (arXiv:2307.05263; https://github.com/PegasusSimulator/PegasusSimulator). BSD-3; requires Isaac Sim.

GPU-native parallel physics and RTX rendering (arXiv:2511.04831). Isaac Sim minimum spec: GeForce RTX 4080, 16 GB VRAM; GPUs without RT cores unsupported (https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/latest/installation/requirements.html). Browser: WebRTC pixel-streaming web viewer via Docker Compose, needs NVENC GPU (https://docs.isaacsim.omniverse.nvidia.com/latest/installation/manual_livestream_clients.html). Isaac Lab code is open; Isaac Sim is under NVIDIA's own licence. No built-in wind field documented.

Open urban layouts created as digital assets (arXiv:1711.03938). Weather (cloud, rain, wind, fog...): 'Changes in the weather do not affect physics. They are only visuals that can be captured by the camera sensors' (https://carla.readthedocs.io/en/latest/core_world/). Determinism with synchronous mode + fixed delta; recorder replay (https://carla.readthedocs.io/en/latest/adv_synchrony_timestep/). No-rendering mode uses no GPU but cameras return empty data (https://carla.readthedocs.io/en/latest/adv_rendering_options/).

Aerial VLN platform integrating Unreal Engine, GTA V, Google Earth and 3D Gaussian Splatting ('real-to-sim'); 18 scenes, 100k trajectories (arXiv:2502.18041). Requires CUDA; UE rendering is 'GPU-intensive' and run headless (https://github.com/SHAILAB-IPEC/OpenFly-Platform). Real geometry only for some scenes.

UE/AirSim-based model of a large Beijing business district; buildings manually modelled in Blender from street-view imagery (not measured point clouds) (https://github.com/tsinghua-fib-lab/EmbodiedCity; arXiv:2410.09604). Online deployment via API key and web console; offline simulator distributed as a Windows binary on Hugging Face.

3D Tiles: OGC Community Standard for 'streaming and rendering massive 3D geospatial content such as Photogrammetry, 3D Buildings ... and Point Clouds' (OGC 22-025r4, https://www.ogc.org/standards/3dtiles/). CesiumJS: Apache-2.0 WebGL library for 3D globes in a web browser (https://github.com/CesiumGS/cesium). Visualisation only; no simulation.

Open-source WebGL renderer for large point clouds (examples up to 18 billion points); deployment is static file hosting, 'not required to install node.js on your webserver' (https://github.com/potree/potree; doi:10.1111/cgf.14134). Visualisation only; no simulation.

Control/estimation/simulation stack aimed at real-world deployment; simulation backends: Gazebo, MRS multirotor simulator, CoppeliaSim, Unreal (https://github.com/ctu-mrs/mrs_uav_system; doi:10.1007/s10846-021-01383-5). Weather/energy/city-scale features not documented in material reviewed.
